# gh-806: [BUG] Rework arming has no in-flight latch — one push spawned 9 arming decisions / 8 silently dead legs (fa PR #1428)

## Description

## Goal

Rework arming in the fa factory must be single-flight and idempotent: for a given (PR, head) at most one rework leg may be in flight, and repeat arming decisions for the same state must dedupe instead of stacking legs.

## Subject

The armer in `machine-sm.yml` tick (`fa`) + the rework leg lifecycle in `preCliReworkSetup.js` / `pushReworkChanges.js` (`dmtools-agents`). Evidence: fa PR #1428, 2026-10-09 04:01–05:04Z window — the tick logged **9 arming decisions for one rework push; 8 legs died silently** (no run, no output) while one leg actually worked. Tick log lines: repeated `✅ pr-1428 agent:rework armed` interleaved with `⏭️ ... nothing to rerun`.

## Capability surface

- Arming decision: tick sees unresolved threads / red verdict → arm rework. Must consult an in-flight latch keyed `(pr-number, head-sha)` before dispatching.
- Latch store: fa-state.json on `factory-data` branch (already persists processedKeys) — extend with `reworkInFlight` map.
- Leg completion: rework leg's post-action must report terminal state (pushed / no-changes / failed) so the tick can clear the latch.
- Silent-death handling: a leg that never produced a run must be re-armable after a bounded timeout (not permanently latched).

## Acceptance criteria

1. AC1: while a rework leg for (pr, head) is in flight, the tick's armer logs `⏭️ rework already in flight for (pr, head)` and dispatches nothing.
2. AC2: after the leg terminates (success or failure), the latch clears and a NEW head (new push) re-arms normally.
3. AC3: a latch older than N=45 min with no matching active workflow run is treated as stale and cleared (self-heal, no human).
4. AC4: duplicate reply passes against already-resolved threads are skipped (idempotency: `pr_discussions_raw.json` entries already RESOLVED are filtered before the agent sees them).
5. AC5: unit test in dmtools-agents for the latch filter; tick-side behavior verified on a live fa PR.

## Test plan

- L1: unit tests on the latch map (set/clear/stale-timeout) and resolved-thread filter.
- L2: replay a recorded arming storm (9 identical decisions) against the filter — exactly 1 dispatch.
- L3 (live): one fa GOAL PR cycle — count rework dispatches per push == 1.

## Non-goals

- Changing review-leg verdict semantics (separate card).
- Parallel rework legs (never a goal — serial by design).

## References

- Forensics: fa PR #1428 round-2 window 04:01–05:04Z 2026-10-09 (9 arms / 8 silent deaths).
- Precedents: dmtools-agents #798 (push race), #799 (rework context prep), #802 (diff-text param).

Must be fixed. - **IMPORTANT** — real maintainability or correctness issue. Strongly prefer fixing before merge. - **SUGGESTION** — optional improvement, style, or future polish. Does not block merge. When in doubt, start one level higher; downgrade only after confirming the risk is negligible. ## 7. Exhaustive single-pass review Treat **every** review as the final and only review pass. The author will not get another chance to catch missed findings cheaply. - Do not defer SUGGESTION or IMPORTANT items to a later round because a BLOCKING issue exists. - After classifying all findings, re-read every changed file and ask: *"What else is improvable here?"* - Before writing outputs, verify that no obvious quality, maintainability, or correctness issue was left unreported. - Aim to surface the maximum number of actionable findings in this single iteration. ## 8. ## PR Description

## Root Cause

The SM tick's rework armers (`js/smAgent.js`: `arm_rework`, `fail_validation` re-arm, `conflict_rework`) had no in-flight latch keyed `(pr, head)` — idempotency relied on the `agent:rework` label plus dispatch-time run guards only, so any suppressed dispatch or silently dead leg left the next tick arming the same state again (fa PR #1428: 9 arms / 8 dead legs for one push). ## Fix

- `js/factoryState.js`: snapshot carries `reworkInFlight` forward and prunes stale/terminated entries each publish (additive; schema unchanged).
- `js/common/gitOps.js`: `writePRContext` filters `resolved === true` threads before writing `pr_discussions_raw.json` (AC4) — single write site, so every agent sees a clean file.

- 53 new tests: `test_reworkLatch.js` (31 — L1 set/clear/stale, L2 nine-decision storm replay → 1 dispatch), `test_factoryState.js` (8 — persistence + pruning), `test_smAgent.js` (11 — AC1/AC2 tick behavior), `test_gitOps.js` (3 — AC4 filter).
- Full suite: **2027 passed, 0 failed** (`dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_all.json`).

## Notes

- Latch clearing is tick-side via the head's Actions runs the tick already queries — no leg-side write; a probe-API failure degrades to age-only checking (fail-safe toward suppressing one extra arm, never toward stacking legs).
- AC5's live check (one fa GOAL PR cycle, dispatches per push == 1) still needs a live factory run; L1/L2 unit coverage is in place.

## PR Description

Closes #806
## Root Cause

The SM tick's rework armers (`js/smAgent.js`: `arm_rework`, `fail_validation` re-arm, `conflict_rework`) had no in-flight latch keyed `(pr, head)` — idempotency relied on the `agent:rework` label plus dispatch-time run guards only, so any suppressed dispatch or silently dead leg left the next tick arming the same state again (fa PR #1428: 9 arms / 8 dead legs for one push). Compounding it, `pr_discussions_raw.json` still contained already-RESOLVED threads, inviting duplicate reply passes.

## Fix

- `js/common/reworkLatch.js` (new, pure): latch keyed `pr-<N>@<head-sha>` — arm at decision time; active leg run keeps it, concluded leg run clears it (AC2), no run + 45 min self-heals (AC3); includes the storm dedupe filter.
- `js/smAgent.js`: all three arming paths consult the latch first and log `⏭️ … rework already in flight for (pr-N, head7)` instead of arming (AC1); arms ride the `factory-data` snapshot out.
- `js/factoryState.js`: snapshot carries `reworkInFlight` forward and prunes stale/terminated entries each publish (additive; schema unchanged).
- `js/common/gitOps.js`: `writePRContext` filters `resolved === true` threads before writing `pr_discussions_raw.json` (AC4) — single write site, so every agent sees a clean file.

## Test Coverage

- 53 new tests: `test_reworkLatch.js` (31 — L1 set/clear/stale, L2 nine-decision storm replay → 1 dispatch), `test_factoryState.js` (8 — persistence + pruning), `test_smAgent.js` (11 — AC1/AC2 tick behavior), `test_gitOps.js` (3 — AC4 filter).
- Full suite: **2027 passed, 0 failed** (`dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_all.json`).

## Notes

- Latch clearing is tick-side via the head's Actions runs the tick already queries — no leg-side write; a probe-API failure degrades to age-only checking (fail-safe toward suppressing one extra arm, never toward stacking legs).
- AC5's live check (one fa GOAL PR cycle, dispatches per push == 1) still needs a live factory run; L1/L2 unit coverage is in place.

# gh-806: [BUG] Rework arming has no in-flight latch — one push spawned 9 arming decisions / 8 silently dead legs (fa PR #1428)

## Description

## Goal

Rework arming in the fa factory must be single-flight and idempotent: for a given (PR, head) at most one rework leg may be in flight, and repeat arming decisions for the same state must dedupe instead of stacking legs.

## Subject

The armer in `machine-sm.yml` tick (`fa`) + the rework leg lifecycle in `preCliReworkSetup.js` / `pushReworkChanges.js` (`dmtools-agents`). Evidence: fa PR #1428, 2026-10-09 04:01–05:04Z window — the tick logged **9 arming decisions for one rework push; 8 legs died silently** (no run, no output) while one leg actually worked. Tick log lines: repeated `✅ pr-1428 agent:rework armed` interleaved with `⏭️ ... nothing to rerun`.

## Capability surface

- Arming decision: tick sees unresolved threads / red verdict → arm rework. Must consult an in-flight latch keyed `(pr-number, head-sha)` before dispatching.
- Latch store: fa-state.json on `factory-data` branch (already persists processedKeys) — extend with `reworkInFlight` map.
- Leg completion: rework leg's post-action must report terminal state (pushed / no-changes / failed) so the tick can clear the latch.
- Silent-death handling: a leg that never produced a run must be re-armable after a bounded timeout (not permanently latched).

## Acceptance criteria

1. AC1: while a rework leg for (pr, head) is in flight, the tick's armer logs `⏭️ rework already in flight for (pr, head)` and dispatches nothing.
2. AC2: after the leg terminates (success or failure), the latch clears and a NEW head (new push) re-arms normally.
3. AC3: a latch older than N=45 min with no matching active workflow run is treated as stale and cleared (self-heal, no human).
4. AC4: duplicate reply passes against already-resolved threads are skipped (idempotency: `pr_discussions_raw.json` entries already RESOLVED are filtered before the agent sees them).
5. AC5: unit test in dmtools-agents for the latch filter; tick-side behavior verified on a live fa PR.

## Test plan

- L1: unit tests on the latch map (set/clear/stale-timeout) and resolved-thread filter.
- L2: replay a recorded arming storm (9 identical decisions) against the filter — exactly 1 dispatch.
- L3 (live): one fa GOAL PR cycle — count rework dispatches per push == 1.

## Non-goals

- Changing review-leg verdict semantics (separate card).
- Parallel rework legs (never a goal — serial by design).

## References

- Forensics: fa PR #1428 round-2 window 04:01–05:04Z 2026-10-09 (9 arms / 8 silent deaths).
- Precedents: dmtools-agents #798 (push race), #799 (rework context prep), #802 (diff-text param).

## PR Description

Closes #806
## Root Cause

The SM tick's rework armers (`js/smAgent.js`: `arm_rework`, `fail_validation` re-arm, `conflict_rework`) had no in-flight latch keyed `(pr, head)` — idempotency relied on the `agent:rework` label plus dispatch-time run guards only, so any suppressed dispatch or silently dead leg left the next tick arming the same state again (fa PR #1428: 9 arms / 8 dead legs for one push). Compounding it, `pr_discussions_raw.json` still contained already-RESOLVED threads, inviting duplicate reply passes.

## Fix

- `js/common/reworkLatch.js` (new, pure): latch keyed `pr-<N>@<head-sha>` — arm at decision time; active leg run keeps it, concluded leg run clears it (AC2), no run + 45 min self-heals (AC3); includes the storm dedupe filter.
- `js/smAgent.js`: all three arming paths consult the latch first and log `⏭️ … rework already in flight for (pr-N, head7)` instead of arming (AC1); arms ride the `factory-data` snapshot out.
- `js/factoryState.js`: snapshot carries `reworkInFlight` forward and prunes stale/terminated entries each publish (additive; schema unchanged).
- `js/common/gitOps.js`: `writePRContext` filters `resolved === true` threads before writing `pr_discussions_raw.json` (AC4) — single write site, so every agent sees a clean file.

## Test Coverage

- 53 new tests: `test_reworkLatch.js` (31 — L1 set/clear/stale, L2 nine-decision storm replay → 1 dispatch), `test_factoryState.js` (8 — persistence + pruning), `test_smAgent.js` (11 — AC1/AC2 tick behavior), `test_gitOps.js` (3 — AC4 filter).
- Full suite: **2027 passed, 0 failed** (`dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_all.json`).

## Notes

- Latch clearing is tick-side via the head's Actions runs the tick already queries — no leg-side write; a probe-API failure degrades to age-only checking (fail-safe toward suppressing one extra arm, never toward stacking legs).
- AC5's live check (one fa GOAL PR cycle, dispatches per push == 1) still needs a live factory run; L1/L2 unit coverage is in place.

# gh-806: [BUG] Rework arming has no in-flight latch — one push spawned 9 arming decisions / 8 silently dead legs (fa PR #1428)

## Description

## Goal

Rework arming in the fa factory must be single-flight and idempotent: for a given (PR, head) at most one rework leg may be in flight, and repeat arming decisions for the same state must dedupe instead of stacking legs.

## Subject

The armer in `machine-sm.yml` tick (`fa`) + the rework leg lifecycle in `preCliReworkSetup.js` / `pushReworkChanges.js` (`dmtools-agents`). Evidence: fa PR #1428, 2026-10-09 04:01–05:04Z window — the tick logged **9 arming decisions for one rework push; 8 legs died silently** (no run, no output) while one leg actually worked. Tick log lines: repeated `✅ pr-1428 agent:rework armed` interleaved with `⏭️ ... nothing to rerun`.

## Capability surface

- Arming decision: tick sees unresolved threads / red verdict → arm rework. Must consult an in-flight latch keyed `(pr-number, head-sha)` before dispatching.
- Latch store: fa-state.json on `factory-data` branch (already persists processedKeys) — extend with `reworkInFlight` map.
- Leg completion: rework leg's post-action must report terminal state (pushed / no-changes / failed) so the tick can clear the latch.
- Silent-death handling: a leg that never produced a run must be re-armable after a bounded timeout (not permanently latched).

## Acceptance criteria

1. AC1: while a rework leg for (pr, head) is in flight, the tick's armer logs `⏭️ rework already in flight for (pr, head)` and dispatches nothing.
2. AC2: after the leg terminates (success or failure), the latch clears and a NEW head (new push) re-arms normally.
3. AC3: a latch older than N=45 min with no matching active workflow run is treated as stale and cleared (self-heal, no human).
4. AC4: duplicate reply passes against already-resolved threads are skipped (idempotency: `pr_discussions_raw.json` entries already RESOLVED are filtered before the agent sees them).
5. AC5: unit test in dmtools-agents for the latch filter; tick-side behavior verified on a live fa PR.

## Test plan

- L1: unit tests on the latch map (set/clear/stale-timeout) and resolved-thread filter.
- L2: replay a recorded arming storm (9 identical decisions) against the filter — exactly 1 dispatch.
- L3 (live): one fa GOAL PR cycle — count rework dispatches per push == 1.

## Non-goals

- Changing review-leg verdict semantics (separate card).
- Parallel rework legs (never a goal — serial by design).

## References

- Forensics: fa PR #1428 round-2 window 04:01–05:04Z 2026-10-09 (9 arms / 8 silent deaths).
- Precedents: dmtools-agents #798 (push race), #799 (rework context prep), #802 (diff-text param).

# Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 811
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/dmtools-agents/pull/811
- **Title**: gh-806 [BUG] Rework arming has no in-flight latch — one push spawned 9 arming decisions / 8 silently dead legs (fa PR #1428)
- **Author**: ai-teammate
- **Branch**: `ai/gh-806` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 10

- **Deletions**: -21

- **Updated**: 2026-10-09T07:21:01Z

## PR Description

Closes #806
## Root Cause

The SM tick's rework armers (`js/smAgent.js`: `arm_rework`, `fail_validation` re-arm, `conflict_rework`) had no in-flight latch keyed `(pr, head)` — idempotency relied on the `agent:rework` label plus dispatch-time run guards only, so any suppressed dispatch or silently dead leg left the next tick arming the same state again (fa PR #1428: 9 arms / 8 dead legs for one push). Compounding it, `pr_discussions_raw.json` still contained already-RESOLVED threads, inviting duplicate reply passes.

## Fix

- `js/common/reworkLatch.js` (new, pure): latch keyed `pr-<N>@<head-sha>` — arm at decision time; active leg run keeps it, concluded leg run clears it (AC2), no run + 45 min self-heals (AC3); includes the storm dedupe filter.
- `js/smAgent.js`: all three arming paths consult the latch first and log `⏭️ … rework already in flight for (pr-N, head7)` instead of arming (AC1); arms ride the `factory-data` snapshot out.
- `js/factoryState.js`: snapshot carries `reworkInFlight` forward and prunes stale/terminated entries each publish (additive; schema unchanged).
- `js/common/gitOps.js`: `writePRContext` filters `resolved === true` threads before writing `pr_discussions_raw.json` (AC4) — single write site, so every agent sees a clean file.

## Test Coverage

- 53 new tests: `test_reworkLatch.js` (31 — L1 set/clear/stale, L2 nine-decision storm replay → 1 dispatch), `test_factoryState.js` (8 — persistence + pruning), `test_smAgent.js` (11 — AC1/AC2 tick behavior), `test_gitOps.js` (3 — AC4 filter).
- Full suite: **2027 passed, 0 failed** (`dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_all.json`).

## Notes

- Latch clearing is tick-side via the head's Actions runs the tick already queries — no leg-side write; a probe-API failure degrades to age-only checking (fail-safe toward suppressing one extra arm, never toward stacking legs).
- AC5's live check (one fa GOAL PR cycle, dispatches per push == 1) still needs a live factory run; L1/L2 unit coverage is in place.

# gh-806: [BUG] Rework arming has no in-flight latch — one push spawned 9 arming decisions / 8 silently dead legs (fa PR #1428)

## Description

## Goal

Rework arming in the fa factory must be single-flight and idempotent: for a given (PR, head) at most one rework leg may be in flight, and repeat arming decisions for the same state must dedupe instead of stacking legs.

## Subject

The armer in `machine-sm.yml` tick (`fa`) + the rework leg lifecycle in `preCliReworkSetup.js` / `pushReworkChanges.js` (`dmtools-agents`). Evidence: fa PR #1428, 2026-10-09 04:01–05:04Z window — the tick logged **9 arming decisions for one rework push; 8 legs died silently** (no run, no output) while one leg actually worked. Tick log lines: repeated `✅ pr-1428 agent:rework armed` interleaved with `⏭️ ... nothing to rerun`.

## Capability surface

- Arming decision: tick sees unresolved threads / red verdict → arm rework. Must consult an in-flight latch keyed `(pr-number, head-sha)` before dispatching.
- Latch store: fa-state.json on `factory-data` branch (already persists processedKeys) — extend with `reworkInFlight` map.
- Leg completion: rework leg's post-action must report terminal state (pushed / no-changes / failed) so the tick can clear the latch.
- Silent-death handling: a leg that never produced a run must be re-armable after a bounded timeout (not permanently latched).

## Acceptance criteria

1. AC1: while a rework leg for (pr, head) is in flight, the tick's armer logs `⏭️ rework already in flight for (pr, head)` and dispatches nothing.
2. AC2: after the leg terminates (success or failure), the latch clears and a NEW head (new push) re-arms normally.
3. AC3: a latch older than N=45 min with no matching active workflow run is treated as stale and cleared (self-heal, no human).
4. AC4: duplicate reply passes against already-resolved threads are skipped (idempotency: `pr_discussions_raw.json` entries already RESOLVED are filtered before the agent sees them).
5. AC5: unit test in dmtools-agents for the latch filter; tick-side behavior verified on a live fa PR.

## Test plan

- L1: unit tests on the latch map (set/clear/stale-timeout) and resolved-thread filter.
- L2: replay a recorded arming storm (9 identical decisions) against the filter — exactly 1 dispatch.
- L3 (live): one fa GOAL PR cycle — count rework dispatches per push == 1.

## Non-goals

- Changing review-leg verdict semantics (separate card).
- Parallel rework legs (never a goal — serial by design).

## References

- Forensics: fa PR #1428 round-2 window 04:01–05:04Z 2026-10-09 (9 arms / 8 silent deaths).
- Precedents: dmtools-agents #798 (push race), #799 (rework context prep), #802 (diff-text param).

Read ticket files to understand WHY it changed and verify against requirements. ## 2. Diff checklist — apply to `pr_diff.txt` For every hunk, ask at least these questions: - [ ] Does the change match the ticket scope? Any scope creep? - [ ] Are new or changed public APIs contract-safe for existing callers? - [ ] Is user/external input validated, sanitized, or escaped? - [ ] Are secrets, tokens, or PATs handled safely — not logged, not interpolated into shell scripts? - [ ] Are new or modified files present under `testing/` in a non-test-automation PR? - [ ] Is dead code, unused imports, or obvious duplication introduced? - [ ] Are error paths handled, or are failures silently swallowed? - [ ] Are new dependencies justified and compatible with the existing stack? - [ ] Beyond blockers: what other maintainability, correctness, or quality improvements are visible in the changed code? ## 3. Does not block merge. When in doubt, start one level higher; downgrade only after confirming the risk is negligible. ## 7. Exhaustive single-pass review Treat **every** review as the final and only review pass. The author will not get another chance to catch missed findings cheaply. - Do not defer SUGGESTION or IMPORTANT items to a later round because a BLOCKING issue exists. - After classifying all findings, re-read every changed file and ask: *"What else is improvable here?"* - Before writing outputs, verify that no obvious quality, maintainability, or correctness issue was left unreported. - Aim to surface the maximum number of actionable findings in this single iteration. ## 8. # gh-806: [BUG] Rework arming has no in-flight latch — one push spawned 9 arming decisions / 8 silently dead legs (fa PR #1428)

## Description

## Goal

Rework arming in the fa factory must be single-flight and idempotent: for a given (PR, head) at most one rework leg may be in flight, and repeat arming decisions for the same state must dedupe instead of stacking legs.

## Subject

The armer in `machine-sm.yml` tick (`fa`) + the rework leg lifecycle in `preCliReworkSetup.js` / `pushReworkChanges.js` (`dmtools-agents`). Evidence: fa PR #1428, 2026-10-09 04:01–05:04Z window — the tick logged **9 arming decisions for one rework push; 8 legs died silently** (no run, no output) while one leg actually worked. Tick log lines: repeated `✅ pr-1428 agent:rework armed` interleaved with `⏭️ ... nothing to rerun`.

## Capability surface

- Arming decision: tick sees unresolved threads / red verdict → arm rework. Must consult an in-flight latch keyed `(pr-number, head-sha)` before dispatching.

- **Author**: ai-teammate
- **Branch**: `ai/gh-806` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 10

- **Updated**: 2026-10-09T07:21:01Z

## PR Description

Closes #806
## Root Cause

The SM tick's rework armers (`js/smAgent.js`: `arm_rework`, `fail_validation` re-arm, `conflict_rework`) had no in-flight latch keyed `(pr, head)` — idempotency relied on the `agent:rework` label plus dispatch-time run guards only, so any suppressed dispatch or silently dead leg left the next tick arming the same state again (fa PR #1428: 9 arms / 8 dead legs for one push). Compounding it, `pr_discussions_raw.json` still contained already-RESOLVED threads, inviting duplicate reply passes.

## Fix

- `js/common/reworkLatch.js` (new, pure): latch keyed `pr-<N>@<head-sha>` — arm at decision time; active leg run keeps it, concluded leg run clears it (AC2), no run + 45 min self-heals (AC3); includes the storm dedupe filter.
- `js/smAgent.js`: all three arming paths consult the latch first and log `⏭️ … rework already in flight for (pr-N, head7)` instead of arming (AC1); arms ride the `factory-data` snapshot out.
- `js/factoryState.js`: snapshot carries `reworkInFlight` forward and prunes stale/terminated entries each publish (additive; schema unchanged).
- `js/common/gitOps.js`: `writePRContext` filters `resolved === true` threads before writing `pr_discussions_raw.json` (AC4) — single write site, so every agent sees a clean file.

## Test Coverage

- 53 new tests: `test_reworkLatch.js` (31 — L1 set/clear/stale, L2 nine-decision storm replay → 1 dispatch), `test_factoryState.js` (8 — persistence + pruning), `test_smAgent.js` (11 — AC1/AC2 tick behavior), `test_gitOps.js` (3 — AC4 filter).
- Full suite: **2027 passed, 0 failed** (`dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_all.json`).

## Notes

- Latch clearing is tick-side via the head's Actions runs the tick already queries — no leg-side write; a probe-API failure degrades to age-only checking (fail-safe toward suppressing one extra arm, never toward stacking legs).
- AC5's live check (one fa GOAL PR cycle, dispatches per push == 1) still needs a live factory run; L1/L2 unit coverage is in place.

# gh-806: [BUG] Rework arming has no in-flight latch — one push spawned 9 arming decisions / 8 silently dead legs (fa PR #1428)

## Description

## Goal

Rework arming in the fa factory must be single-flight and idempotent: for a given (PR, head) at most one rework leg may be in flight, and repeat arming decisions for the same state must dedupe instead of stacking legs.

## Subject

The armer in `machine-sm.yml` tick (`fa`) + the rework leg lifecycle in `preCliReworkSetup.js` / `pushReworkChanges.js` (`dmtools-agents`). Evidence: fa PR #1428, 2026-10-09 04:01–05:04Z window — the tick logged **9 arming decisions for one rework push; 8 legs died silently** (no run, no output) while one leg actually worked. Tick log lines: repeated `✅ pr-1428 agent:rework armed` interleaved with `⏭️ ... nothing to rerun`.

## Capability surface

- Arming decision: tick sees unresolved threads / red verdict → arm rework. Must consult an in-flight latch keyed `(pr-number, head-sha)` before dispatching.
- Latch store: fa-state.json on `factory-data` branch (already persists processedKeys) — extend with `reworkInFlight` map.
- Leg completion: rework leg's post-action must report terminal state (pushed / no-changes / failed) so the tick can clear the latch.
- Silent-death handling: a leg that never produced a run must be re-armable after a bounded timeout (not permanently latched).

## Acceptance criteria

1. AC1: while a rework leg for (pr, head) is in flight, the tick's armer logs `⏭️ rework already in flight for (pr, head)` and dispatches nothing.
2. AC2: after the leg terminates (success or failure), the latch clears and a NEW head (new push) re-arms normally.
3. AC3: a latch older than N=45 min with no matching active workflow run is treated as stale and cleared (self-heal, no human).
4. AC4: duplicate reply passes against already-resolved threads are skipped (idempotency: `pr_discussions_raw.json` entries already RESOLVED are filtered before the agent sees them).
5. AC5: unit test in dmtools-agents for the latch filter; tick-side behavior verified on a live fa PR.

## Test plan

- L1: unit tests on the latch map (set/clear/stale-timeout) and resolved-thread filter.
- L2: replay a recorded arming storm (9 identical decisions) against the filter — exactly 1 dispatch.
- L3 (live): one fa GOAL PR cycle — count rework dispatches per push == 1.

## Non-goals

- Changing review-leg verdict semantics (separate card).
- Parallel rework legs (never a goal — serial by design).

## References

- Forensics: fa PR #1428 round-2 window 04:01–05:04Z 2026-10-09 (9 arms / 8 silent deaths).
- Precedents: dmtools-agents #798 (push race), #799 (rework context prep), #802 (diff-text param).

- **Author**: ai-teammate

- **Updated**: 2026-10-09T07:21:01Z

## PR Description

Closes #806
## Root Cause

The SM tick's rework armers (`js/smAgent.js`: `arm_rework`, `fail_validation` re-arm, `conflict_rework`) had no in-flight latch keyed `(pr, head)` — idempotency relied on the `agent:rework` label plus dispatch-time run guards only, so any suppressed dispatch or silently dead leg left the next tick arming the same state again (fa PR #1428: 9 arms / 8 dead legs for one push). Compounding it, `pr_discussions_raw.json` still contained already-RESOLVED threads, inviting duplicate reply passes.

## Fix

- `js/common/reworkLatch.js` (new, pure): latch keyed `pr-<N>@<head-sha>` — arm at decision time; active leg run keeps it, concluded leg run clears it (AC2), no run + 45 min self-heals (AC3); includes the storm dedupe filter.
- `js/smAgent.js`: all three arming paths consult the latch first and log `⏭️ … rework already in flight for (pr-N, head7)` instead of arming (AC1); arms ride the `factory-data` snapshot out.
- `js/factoryState.js`: snapshot carries `reworkInFlight` forward and prunes stale/terminated entries each publish (additive; schema unchanged).
- `js/common/gitOps.js`: `writePRContext` filters `resolved === true` threads before writing `pr_discussions_raw.json` (AC4) — single write site, so every agent sees a clean file.

## Test Coverage

- 53 new tests: `test_reworkLatch.js` (31 — L1 set/clear/stale, L2 nine-decision storm replay → 1 dispatch), `test_factoryState.js` (8 — persistence + pruning), `test_smAgent.js` (11 — AC1/AC2 tick behavior), `test_gitOps.js` (3 — AC4 filter).
- Full suite: **2027 passed, 0 failed** (`dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_all.json`).

## Notes

- Latch clearing is tick-side via the head's Actions runs the tick already queries — no leg-side write; a probe-API failure degrades to age-only checking (fail-safe toward suppressing one extra arm, never toward stacking legs).
- AC5's live check (one fa GOAL PR cycle, dispatches per push == 1) still needs a live factory run; L1/L2 unit coverage is in place.

# gh-806: [BUG] Rework arming has no in-flight latch — one push spawned 9 arming decisions / 8 silently dead legs (fa PR #1428)

## Description

## Goal

Rework arming in the fa factory must be single-flight and idempotent: for a given (PR, head) at most one rework leg may be in flight, and repeat arming decisions for the same state must dedupe instead of stacking legs.

## Subject

The armer in `machine-sm.yml` tick (`fa`) + the rework leg lifecycle in `preCliReworkSetup.js` / `pushReworkChanges.js` (`dmtools-agents`). Evidence: fa PR #1428, 2026-10-09 04:01–05:04Z window — the tick logged **9 arming decisions for one rework push; 8 legs died silently** (no run, no output) while one leg actually worked. Tick log lines: repeated `✅ pr-1428 agent:rework armed` interleaved with `⏭️ ... nothing to rerun`.

## Capability surface

- Arming decision: tick sees unresolved threads / red verdict → arm rework. Must consult an in-flight latch keyed `(pr-number, head-sha)` before dispatching.
- Latch store: fa-state.json on `factory-data` branch (already persists processedKeys) — extend with `reworkInFlight` map.
- Leg completion: rework leg's post-action must report terminal state (pushed / no-changes / failed) so the tick can clear the latch.
- Silent-death handling: a leg that never produced a run must be re-armable after a bounded timeout (not permanently latched).

## Acceptance criteria

1. AC1: while a rework leg for (pr, head) is in flight, the tick's armer logs `⏭️ rework already in flight for (pr, head)` and dispatches nothing.
2. AC2: after the leg terminates (success or failure), the latch clears and a NEW head (new push) re-arms normally.
3. AC3: a latch older than N=45 min with no matching active workflow run is treated as stale and cleared (self-heal, no human).
4. AC4: duplicate reply passes against already-resolved threads are skipped (idempotency: `pr_discussions_raw.json` entries already RESOLVED are filtered before the agent sees them).
5. AC5: unit test in dmtools-agents for the latch filter; tick-side behavior verified on a live fa PR.

## Test plan

- L1: unit tests on the latch map (set/clear/stale-timeout) and resolved-thread filter.
- L2: replay a recorded arming storm (9 identical decisions) against the filter — exactly 1 dispatch.
- L3 (live): one fa GOAL PR cycle — count rework dispatches per push == 1.

## Non-goals

- Changing review-leg verdict semantics (separate card).
- Parallel rework legs (never a goal — serial by design).

## References

- Forensics: fa PR #1428 round-2 window 04:01–05:04Z 2026-10-09 (9 arms / 8 silent deaths).
- Precedents: dmtools-agents #798 (push race), #799 (rework context prep), #802 (diff-text param).

## PR Description

Closes #806
## Root Cause

The SM tick's rework armers (`js/smAgent.js`: `arm_rework`, `fail_validation` re-arm, `conflict_rework`) had no in-flight latch keyed `(pr, head)` — idempotency relied on the `agent:rework` label plus dispatch-time run guards only, so any suppressed dispatch or silently dead leg left the next tick arming the same state again (fa PR #1428: 9 arms / 8 dead legs for one push). Compounding it, `pr_discussions_raw.json` still contained already-RESOLVED threads, inviting duplicate reply passes.

## Fix

- `js/common/reworkLatch.js` (new, pure): latch keyed `pr-<N>@<head-sha>` — arm at decision time; active leg run keeps it, concluded leg run clears it (AC2), no run + 45 min self-heals (AC3); includes the storm dedupe filter.
- `js/smAgent.js`: all three arming paths consult the latch first and log `⏭️ … rework already in flight for (pr-N, head7)` instead of arming (AC1); arms ride the `factory-data` snapshot out.
- `js/factoryState.js`: snapshot carries `reworkInFlight` forward and prunes stale/terminated entries each publish (additive; schema unchanged).
- `js/common/gitOps.js`: `writePRContext` filters `resolved === true` threads before writing `pr_discussions_raw.json` (AC4) — single write site, so every agent sees a clean file.

## Test Coverage

- 53 new tests: `test_reworkLatch.js` (31 — L1 set/clear/stale, L2 nine-decision storm replay → 1 dispatch), `test_factoryState.js` (8 — persistence + pruning), `test_smAgent.js` (11 — AC1/AC2 tick behavior), `test_gitOps.js` (3 — AC4 filter).
- Full suite: **2027 passed, 0 failed** (`dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_all.json`).

## Notes

- Latch clearing is tick-side via the head's Actions runs the tick already queries — no leg-side write; a probe-API failure degrades to age-only checking (fail-safe toward suppressing one extra arm, never toward stacking legs).
- AC5's live check (one fa GOAL PR cycle, dispatches per push == 1) still needs a live factory run; L1/L2 unit coverage is in place.

# gh-806: [BUG] Rework arming has no in-flight latch — one push spawned 9 arming decisions / 8 silently dead legs (fa PR #1428)

## Description

## Goal

Rework arming in the fa factory must be single-flight and idempotent: for a given (PR, head) at most one rework leg may be in flight, and repeat arming decisions for the same state must dedupe instead of stacking legs.

## Subject

The armer in `machine-sm.yml` tick (`fa`) + the rework leg lifecycle in `preCliReworkSetup.js` / `pushReworkChanges.js` (`dmtools-agents`). Evidence: fa PR #1428, 2026-10-09 04:01–05:04Z window — the tick logged **9 arming decisions for one rework push; 8 legs died silently** (no run, no output) while one leg actually worked. Tick log lines: repeated `✅ pr-1428 agent:rework armed` interleaved with `⏭️ ... nothing to rerun`.

## Capability surface

- Arming decision: tick sees unresolved threads / red verdict → arm rework. Must consult an in-flight latch keyed `(pr-number, head-sha)` before dispatching.
- Latch store: fa-state.json on `factory-data` branch (already persists processedKeys) — extend with `reworkInFlight` map.
- Leg completion: rework leg's post-action must report terminal state (pushed / no-changes / failed) so the tick can clear the latch.
- Silent-death handling: a leg that never produced a run must be re-armable after a bounded timeout (not permanently latched).

## Acceptance criteria

1. AC1: while a rework leg for (pr, head) is in flight, the tick's armer logs `⏭️ rework already in flight for (pr, head)` and dispatches nothing.
2. AC2: after the leg terminates (success or failure), the latch clears and a NEW head (new push) re-arms normally.
3. AC3: a latch older than N=45 min with no matching active workflow run is treated as stale and cleared (self-heal, no human).
4. AC4: duplicate reply passes against already-resolved threads are skipped (idempotency: `pr_discussions_raw.json` entries already RESOLVED are filtered before the agent sees them).
5. AC5: unit test in dmtools-agents for the latch filter; tick-side behavior verified on a live fa PR.

## Test plan

- L1: unit tests on the latch map (set/clear/stale-timeout) and resolved-thread filter.
- L2: replay a recorded arming storm (9 identical decisions) against the filter — exactly 1 dispatch.
- L3 (live): one fa GOAL PR cycle — count rework dispatches per push == 1.

## Non-goals

- Changing review-leg verdict semantics (separate card).
- Parallel rework legs (never a goal — serial by design).

## References

- Forensics: fa PR #1428 round-2 window 04:01–05:04Z 2026-10-09 (9 arms / 8 silent deaths).
- Precedents: dmtools-agents #798 (push race), #799 (rework context prep), #802 (diff-text param).

## PR Description

Closes #806
## Root Cause

The SM tick's rework armers (`js/smAgent.js`: `arm_rework`, `fail_validation` re-arm, `conflict_rework`) had no in-flight latch keyed `(pr, head)` — idempotency relied on the `agent:rework` label plus dispatch-time run guards only, so any suppressed dispatch or silently dead leg left the next tick arming the same state again (fa PR #1428: 9 arms / 8 dead legs for one push). Compounding it, `pr_discussions_raw.json` still contained already-RESOLVED threads, inviting duplicate reply passes.

## Fix

- `js/common/reworkLatch.js` (new, pure): latch keyed `pr-<N>@<head-sha>` — arm at decision time; active leg run keeps it, concluded leg run clears it (AC2), no run + 45 min self-heals (AC3); includes the storm dedupe filter.
- `js/smAgent.js`: all three arming paths consult the latch first and log `⏭️ … rework already in flight for (pr-N, head7)` instead of arming (AC1); arms ride the `factory-data` snapshot out.
- `js/factoryState.js`: snapshot carries `reworkInFlight` forward and prunes stale/terminated entries each publish (additive; schema unchanged).
- `js/common/gitOps.js`: `writePRContext` filters `resolved === true` threads before writing `pr_discussions_raw.json` (AC4) — single write site, so every agent sees a clean file.

## Test Coverage

- 53 new tests: `test_reworkLatch.js` (31 — L1 set/clear/stale, L2 nine-decision storm replay → 1 dispatch), `test_factoryState.js` (8 — persistence + pruning), `test_smAgent.js` (11 — AC1/AC2 tick behavior), `test_gitOps.js` (3 — AC4 filter).
- Full suite: **2027 passed, 0 failed** (`dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_all.json`).

## Notes

- Latch clearing is tick-side via the head's Actions runs the tick already queries — no leg-side write; a probe-API failure degrades to age-only checking (fail-safe toward suppressing one extra arm, never toward stacking legs).
- AC5's live check (one fa GOAL PR cycle, dispatches per push == 1) still needs a live factory run; L1/L2 unit coverage is in place.

# gh-806: [BUG] Rework arming has no in-flight latch — one push spawned 9 arming decisions / 8 silently dead legs (fa PR #1428)

## Description

## Goal

Rework arming in the fa factory must be single-flight and idempotent: for a given (PR, head) at most one rework leg may be in flight, and repeat arming decisions for the same state must dedupe instead of stacking legs.

## Subject

The armer in `machine-sm.yml` tick (`fa`) + the rework leg lifecycle in `preCliReworkSetup.js` / `pushReworkChanges.js` (`dmtools-agents`). Evidence: fa PR #1428, 2026-10-09 04:01–05:04Z window — the tick logged **9 arming decisions for one rework push; 8 legs died silently** (no run, no output) while one leg actually worked. Tick log lines: repeated `✅ pr-1428 agent:rework armed` interleaved with `⏭️ ... nothing to rerun`.

## Capability surface

- Arming decision: tick sees unresolved threads / red verdict → arm rework. Must consult an in-flight latch keyed `(pr-number, head-sha)` before dispatching.
- Latch store: fa-state.json on `factory-data` branch (already persists processedKeys) — extend with `reworkInFlight` map.
- Leg completion: rework leg's post-action must report terminal state (pushed / no-changes / failed) so the tick can clear the latch.
- Silent-death handling: a leg that never produced a run must be re-armable after a bounded timeout (not permanently latched).

## Acceptance criteria

1. AC1: while a rework leg for (pr, head) is in flight, the tick's armer logs `⏭️ rework already in flight for (pr, head)` and dispatches nothing.
2. AC2: after the leg terminates (success or failure), the latch clears and a NEW head (new push) re-arms normally.
3. AC3: a latch older than N=45 min with no matching active workflow run is treated as stale and cleared (self-heal, no human).
4. AC4: duplicate reply passes against already-resolved threads are skipped (idempotency: `pr_discussions_raw.json` entries already RESOLVED are filtered before the agent sees them).
5. AC5: unit test in dmtools-agents for the latch filter; tick-side behavior verified on a live fa PR.

## Test plan

- L1: unit tests on the latch map (set/clear/stale-timeout) and resolved-thread filter.
- L2: replay a recorded arming storm (9 identical decisions) against the filter — exactly 1 dispatch.
- L3 (live): one fa GOAL PR cycle — count rework dispatches per push == 1.

## Non-goals

- Changing review-leg verdict semantics (separate card).
- Parallel rework legs (never a goal — serial by design).

## References

- Forensics: fa PR #1428 round-2 window 04:01–05:04Z 2026-10-09 (9 arms / 8 silent deaths).
- Precedents: dmtools-agents #798 (push race), #799 (rework context prep), #802 (diff-text param).

So `processedKeys` is a per-tick list, only used for limit enforcement (`processedKeys.length >= effectiveLimit`) and the snapshot's `tick.processed`. Within a rule, each ticket appears once, so pushing or not pushing on suppression only affects the limit counter (how many slots the rule consumed) and the snapshot record. Not a correctness issue.

Now the snapshot side. Let me re-examine `buildFactoryState`'s prune call more carefully:

```js
var reworkInFlight = reworkLatchModule.pruneStale(
    reworkLatchModule.normalizeMap(latchCarry), {
        now: nowMs,
        runs: runs,
        workflowFile: input.legWorkflow
    }).map;
```

Wait — `now: nowMs` — `nowMs = Date.parse(now)`. `nowMsOf(opts)` → `toMs(opts.now)` — number → returned as-is. OK.

`runs` = `input.runs` = the repo-wide `github_list_workflow_runs` (perPage 50). Note in `evaluate` → `latchEffectOfRun(run, entry.head, atMs, workflowFile)`:

- isLegRun: path suffix match on leg workflow.
- head mismatch → null.
- active status → 'in-flight'.
- completed && endedMs >= entryAtMs → 'terminated'.

Consideration: **entries whose leg run is completed BEFORE the arm** — none (arm precedes dispatch). 

But here's a subtle one: **the run rollup in the publish path is repo-wide, capped at 50**. `evaluate` with `runs` given: if any leg run on the head is ACTIVE → 'in-flight' — kept even past stale. If a leg run concluded after arm → 'terminated' → pruned. Good. If the run list doesn't include the head's run (older than 50) → falls back to age-only. OK.

**Important issue candidate — `pruneStale` at publish vs `tickReworkLatch.map` in the same tick:** the publish block builds `spPrev` via `fetchPreviousState`, merges `prev.reworkInFlight` + live `tickReworkLatch.map`, prunes, and stores in the snapshot. But `tickReworkLatch` itself (in-memory) is NOT updated with the pruned map. Within a single tick this doesn't matter (publish happens at the end). OK.

**Bigger issue candidate — the latch clear path never persists mid-tick:** `consultReworkLatch` clears entries in the in-memory map; the cleared state rides out only via the publish at end of tick. If publishing fails or is not configured, the latch stays in the snapshot (on the branch) and the next tick re-loads it. But then the next tick re-consults: entry present → probe runs → terminated → cleared again. Self-healing each tick — no wedge. OK.

**Now the real question — AC2 clearing when the leg TERMINATES but the tick doesn't run for a while:** fine.

**What about the review-leg latch?** The latch module comment says the same `ai-teammate.yml` workflow is used by review legs. So a REVIEW leg run on the head also counts as 'in-flight' latch keeper and its conclusion clears the latch. Is that a problem? The latch is armed only by rework arming paths. If a review leg for the same (pr, head) is flying and the tick arms rework (e.g. unresolved threads appear while review in flight?), the arm records the latch; the review leg's conclusion would clear the rework latch even though no rework leg ever ran. Consequence: rework re-arms next tick — that's the pre-gateway behavior; acceptable (fail-open to re-arm, not stacking). Hmm, but wait: could that cause an arm-suppress-miss? The arming storm protection dedupes repeated arms per tick via in-memory map. Fine.

**Now — the critical concurrency issue: multiple SM machines/ticks.** The latch state is loaded once per tick from the factory-data snapshot and armed in-memory during the tick; races between two concurrent ticks could double-arm. Same as before for processedKeys; out of scope.

**Check `consultReworkLatch` failure semantics once more:**

```js
var verdict = reworkLatchModule.isActive(latchState.map, prNumber, head, {});
if (verdict.entry) {
    var runs = headWorkflowRunsSafe(effectiveRepoInfo, head);
    verdict = reworkLatchModule.isActive(..., { runs: runs, ... });
}
```

Wait — there's a subtle bug here. `headWorkflowRunsSafe` can return `null` (probe failed) — fine, degrades to age-only. BUT the second `isActive` is called with `runs: null`... `evaluate` checks `Array.isArray(opts.runs)` → null → skip. Good.

But what about `headWorkflowRunsSafe` returning `[]` (empty runs — e.g., the run hasn't been REGISTERED yet — dispatch accepted, run not yet visible)? Then evaluate: runs=[] → no in-flight, no terminated → age check: fresh arm (< 45 min) → 'in-flight'. Suppressed — correct (that's exactly the storm scenario: dispatch accepted but run not materialized; latch keeps it suppressed until the run shows up or 45 min pass). 

**The AC3 window and the arm `at` timestamp:** the arm time is the arming tick's now. A leg dispatched at minute 44, run registered at 46 → between 45 and 46, latch is stale → a second arm could go out (if the arming condition still holds). Rare race, acceptable, bounded.

**Now — `isActive` first call without runs, `verdict.entry` re-probe cost:** For every suppressed arm in a tick, one `gh api` probe per (pr, head) — that's fine.

Hmm wait, actually there's a subtle inefficiency/bug: In the arm_rework path, `consultReworkLatch` is called on EVERY ticket matching arm_rework even when the latch map is EMPTY. `verdict.entry` is null when map has no entry → no probe. Good — zero extra gh calls when no latch entry exists.

**Now check `evaluate` when entry present and runs provided and the head's leg run is active but the run is on a DIFFERENT head than the entry's `entry.head`:** `latchEffectOfRun(run, entry.head, ...)` — uses entry.head (the recorded head), not the queried head. In `consultReworkLatch` they're the same (entryFor(map, prNumber, head) → entry.head === head by construction of arm()). OK.

**`normalizeMap` head vs key consistency:** normalizeMap doesn't verify `key === 'pr-' + ... '@' + entry.head` — e.g., a key 'pr-5@aaa' with entry.head 'bbb' stays. `entryFor` looks up by key, `evaluate` uses entry.head for run matching. A mismatched entry would keep/suppress based on head bbb runs but keyed to pr-5@aaa. Since only `arm()` writes entries, this is only reachable via a hand-corrupted snapshot — normalizeMap's sanitization is "best effort". Minor.

**Now, the `dedupeArms` L2 storm filter — is it actually USED anywhere in production code?** It's exported from reworkLatch and tested, but does smAgent call `dedupeArms`? Let me grep.

re-read changed files,
surface ALL remaining issues"] EXHAUST --> OUTPUT["8. Write outputs:
pr_review.json · pr_review_general.md · pr_review_comments/*.md"] OUTPUT --> END([End]) ``` ## 1. Input context — MANDATORY reading order ```mermaid flowchart TD subgraph PR_CONTEXT["⚠️ PR-specific files (read first)"] P1["1️⃣ instruction.md (repo root) — project stack, conventions"] P2["2️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_info.md — PR title, author, branch, description"] P3["3️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_diff.txt — the diff to review"] P4["4️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_files.txt — list of changed files"] P5["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures.md — CI failures = BLOCKING (last 500 lines)"] P5_FULL["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures_full.log — full CI logs"] P6["6️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_discussions.md + pr_discussions_raw.json — existing comments"] P1 --> P2 --> P3 --> P4 --> P5 --> P5_FULL --> P6 end subgraph TICKET_CONTEXT["Ticket context (for understanding PR purpose)"] T1["7️⃣ input/TICKET/ticket.md — linked ticket description, ACs"] T2["8️⃣ input/TICKET/comments.md — ticket discussion if present"] T3["9️⃣ input/TICKET/parent-*.md — parent story context"] T4["🔟 input/TICKET/confluence/*.md — linked specifications"] T1 --> T2 --> T3 --> T4 end subgraph RULE["⚠️ Rule"] R1["If file exists in input/ → read locally, do NOT re-fetch via dmtools"] end PR_CONTEXT --> TICKET_CONTEXT --> RULE ``` Read PR files to understand WHAT changed. Read ticket files to understand WHY it changed and verify against requirements. ## 2. Diff checklist — apply to `pr_diff.txt` For every hunk, ask at least these questions: - [ ] Does the change match the ticket scope? Any scope creep? - [ ] Are new or changed public APIs contract-safe for existing callers? - [ ] Is user/external input validated, sanitized, or escaped? - [ ] Are secrets, tokens, or PATs handled safely — not logged, not interpolated into shell scripts? - [ ] Are new or modified files present under `testing/` in a non-test-automation PR? - [ ] Is dead code, unused imports, or obvious duplication introduced? - [ ] Are error paths handled, or are failures silently swallowed? - [ ] Are new dependencies justified and compatible with the existing stack? - [ ] Beyond blockers: what other maintainability, correctness, or quality improvements are visible in the changed code? ## 3. Changed-file deep read Do not review from the diff alone. Read the full content of every changed file: - imports and dependencies - class/method responsibilities and adherence to SRP / OOP principles - naming consistency with the rest of the codebase - error handling, logging, and edge cases - test coverage for changed behavior - backward-compatibility and migration impact ## 4. Impact analysis (CodeGraph or grep fallback) Use CodeGraph to find "what could break": - `codegraph_callers` / `codegraph_callees` on modified public symbols - `codegraph_search` for: `PAT_TOKEN`, `secrets.`, `github.token`, `previousViewModel` - `codegraph_impact` before flagging architectural changes **If CodeGraph unavailable**, use grep and document it: ```bash grep -rn "changedFunctionName" --include="*.ts" . grep -rn "secrets\.\|github\.token" . ``` ## 5. Review dimensions Rate the PR across all relevant dimensions: | Dimension | What to check | |---|---| | **Security** | injection, unsafe interpolation, secret leakage, missing permissions, unsafe defaults | | **Architecture / OOP** | SRP, coupling, abstraction consistency, provider/repository boundaries | | **Code quality** | naming, complexity, error handling, logging, comments | | **Tests** | coverage for new/changed paths, meaningful assertions, no brittle string-only tests | | **Duplication** | copy-paste, duplicated logic across files, duplicated configuration | | **Backward compatibility** | public API changes, migration paths, default behavior | | **Performance** | unnecessary rebuilds, heavy sync operations, missing timeouts | | **Workflow / CI safety** | (when `.github/workflows/` changes) secret declarations, ref pinning, permissions, timeouts | ## 6. Severity classification Classify every finding before writing outputs: - **BLOCKING** — merge would cause a bug, security issue, data loss, or CI break. Must be fixed. - **IMPORTANT** — real maintainability or correctness issue. Strongly prefer fixing before merge. - **SUGGESTION** — optional improvement, style, or future polish. Does not block merge. When in doubt, start one level higher; downgrade only after confirming the risk is negligible. ## 7. Exhaustive single-pass review Treat **every** review as the final and only review pass. The author will not get another chance to catch missed findings cheaply. - Do not defer SUGGESTION or IMPORTANT items to a later round because a BLOCKING issue exists. - After classifying all findings, re-read every changed file and ask: *"What else is improvable here?"* - Before writing outputs, verify that no obvious quality, maintainability, or correctness issue was left unreported. - Aim to surface the maximum number of actionable findings in this single iteration. ## 8. Outputs Write the standard review artifacts: - `outputs/pr_review.json` — structured data with `recommendation`, `summary`, `inlineComments`, `issueCounts` - `outputs/pr_review_general.md` — 1-2 paragraph general PR comment - `outputs/pr_review_comments/*.md` — one file per detailed inline comment **Inline comment lines must be present in the PR diff.** GitHub review threads can only be attached to added or context lines inside a diff hunk. If `pr_diff.txt` is truncated, run `git diff origin/{baseBranch}...HEAD` to locate the correct line numbers. Findings on unchanged code outside the diff belong in `outputs/pr_review_general.md`, not as inline comments. Do NOT write `outputs/response.md`; the review is posted to GitHub only. ```mermaid flowchart TD O1["Write outputs/pr_review.json — structured data for GitHub PR review…

## PR Description

Closes #806
## Root Cause

The SM tick's rework armers (`js/smAgent.js`: `arm_rework`, `fail_validation` re-arm, `conflict_rework`) had no in-flight latch keyed `(pr, head)` — idempotency relied on the `agent:rework` label plus dispatch-time run guards only, so any suppressed dispatch or silently dead leg left the next tick arming the same state again (fa PR #1428: 9 arms / 8 dead legs for one push). Compounding it, `pr_discussions_raw.json` still contained already-RESOLVED threads, inviting duplicate reply passes.

## Fix

- `js/common/reworkLatch.js` (new, pure): latch keyed `pr-<N>@<head-sha>` — arm at decision time; active leg run keeps it, concluded leg run clears it (AC2), no run + 45 min self-heals (AC3); includes the storm dedupe filter.
- `js/smAgent.js`: all three arming paths consult the latch first and log `⏭️ … rework already in flight for (pr-N, head7)` instead of arming (AC1); arms ride the `factory-data` snapshot out.
- `js/factoryState.js`: snapshot carries `reworkInFlight` forward and prunes stale/terminated entries each publish (additive; schema unchanged).
- `js/common/gitOps.js`: `writePRContext` filters `resolved === true` threads before writing `pr_discussions_raw.json` (AC4) — single write site, so every agent sees a clean file.

## Test Coverage

- 53 new tests: `test_reworkLatch.js` (31 — L1 set/clear/stale, L2 nine-decision storm replay → 1 dispatch), `test_factoryState.js` (8 — persistence + pruning), `test_smAgent.js` (11 — AC1/AC2 tick behavior), `test_gitOps.js` (3 — AC4 filter).
- Full suite: **2027 passed, 0 failed** (`dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_all.json`).

## Notes

- Latch clearing is tick-side via the head's Actions runs the tick already queries — no leg-side write; a probe-API failure degrades to age-only checking (fail-safe toward suppressing one extra arm, never toward stacking legs).
- AC5's live check (one fa GOAL PR cycle, dispatches per push == 1) still needs a live factory run; L1/L2 unit coverage is in place.

# gh-806: [BUG] Rework arming has no in-flight latch — one push spawned 9 arming decisions / 8 silently dead legs (fa PR #1428)

## Description

## Goal

Rework arming in the fa factory must be single-flight and idempotent: for a given (PR, head) at most one rework leg may be in flight, and repeat arming decisions for the same state must dedupe instead of stacking legs.

## Subject

The armer in `machine-sm.yml` tick (`fa`) + the rework leg lifecycle in `preCliReworkSetup.js` / `pushReworkChanges.js` (`dmtools-agents`). Evidence: fa PR #1428, 2026-10-09 04:01–05:04Z window — the tick logged **9 arming decisions for one rework push; 8 legs died silently** (no run, no output) while one leg actually worked. Tick log lines: repeated `✅ pr-1428 agent:rework armed` interleaved with `⏭️ ... nothing to rerun`.

## Capability surface

- Arming decision: tick sees unresolved threads / red verdict → arm rework. Must consult an in-flight latch keyed `(pr-number, head-sha)` before dispatching.
- Latch store: fa-state.json on `factory-data` branch (already persists processedKeys) — extend with `reworkInFlight` map.
- Leg completion: rework leg's post-action must report terminal state (pushed / no-changes / failed) so the tick can clear the latch.
- Silent-death handling: a leg that never produced a run must be re-armable after a bounded timeout (not permanently latched).

## Acceptance criteria

1. AC1: while a rework leg for (pr, head) is in flight, the tick's armer logs `⏭️ rework already in flight for (pr, head)` and dispatches nothing.
2. AC2: after the leg terminates (success or failure), the latch clears and a NEW head (new push) re-arms normally.
3. AC3: a latch older than N=45 min with no matching active workflow run is treated as stale and cleared (self-heal, no human).
4. AC4: duplicate reply passes against already-resolved threads are skipped (idempotency: `pr_discussions_raw.json` entries already RESOLVED are filtered before the agent sees them).
5. AC5: unit test in dmtools-agents for the latch filter; tick-side behavior verified on a live fa PR.

## Test plan

- L1: unit tests on the latch map (set/clear/stale-timeout) and resolved-thread filter.
- L2: replay a recorded arming storm (9 identical decisions) against the filter — exactly 1 dispatch.
- L3 (live): one fa GOAL PR cycle — count rework dispatches per push == 1.

## Non-goals

- Changing review-leg verdict semantics (separate card).
- Parallel rework legs (never a goal — serial by design).

## References

- Forensics: fa PR #1428 round-2 window 04:01–05:04Z 2026-10-09 (9 arms / 8 silent deaths).
- Precedents: dmtools-agents #798 (push race), #799 (rework context prep), #802 (diff-text param).

# Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 811
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/dmtools-agents/pull/811
- **Title**: gh-806 [BUG] Rework arming has no in-flight latch — one push spawned 9 arming decisions / 8 silently dead legs (fa PR #1428)
- **Author**: ai-teammate
- **Branch**: `ai/gh-806` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 10
- **Additions**: +1282
- **Deletions**: -21
- **Created**: 2026-10-09T07:21:01Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-09T07:21:01Z

## PR Description

Closes #806
## Root Cause

The SM tick's rework armers (`js/smAgent.js`: `arm_rework`, `fail_validation` re-arm, `conflict_rework`) had no in-flight latch keyed `(pr, head)` — idempotency relied on the `agent:rework` label plus dispatch-time run guards only, so any suppressed dispatch or silently dead leg left the next tick arming the same state again (fa PR #1428: 9 arms / 8 dead legs for one push). Compounding it, `pr_discussions_raw.json` still contained already-RESOLVED threads, inviting duplicate reply passes.

## Fix

- `js/common/reworkLatch.js` (new, pure): latch keyed `pr-<N>@<head-sha>` — arm at decision time; active leg run keeps it, concluded leg run clears it (AC2), no run + 45 min self-heals (AC3); includes the storm dedupe filter.
- `js/smAgent.js`: all three arming paths consult the latch first and log `⏭️ … rework already in flight for (pr-N, head7)` instead of arming (AC1); arms ride the `factory-data` snapshot out.
- `js/factoryState.js`: snapshot carries `reworkInFlight` forward and prunes stale/terminated entries each publish (additive; schema unchanged).
- `js/common/gitOps.js`: `writePRContext` filters `resolved === true` threads before writing `pr_discussions_raw.json` (AC4) — single write site, so every agent sees a clean file.

## Test Coverage

- 53 new tests: `test_reworkLatch.js` (31 — L1 set/clear/stale, L2 nine-decision storm replay → 1 dispatch), `test_factoryState.js` (8 — persistence + pruning), `test_smAgent.js` (11 — AC1/AC2 tick behavior), `test_gitOps.js` (3 — AC4 filter).
- Full suite: **2027 passed, 0 failed** (`dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_all.json`).

## Notes

- Latch clearing is tick-side via the head's Actions runs the tick already queries — no leg-side write; a probe-API failure degrades to age-only checking (fail-safe toward suppressing one extra arm, never toward stacking legs).

# gh-806: [BUG] Rework arming has no in-flight latch — one push spawned 9 arming decisions / 8 silently dead legs (fa PR #1428)

## Description

## Goal

Rework arming in the fa factory must be single-flight and idempotent: for a given (PR, head) at most one rework leg may be in flight, and repeat arming decisions for the same state must dedupe instead of stacking legs.

## Subject

The armer in `machine-sm.yml` tick (`fa`) + the rework leg lifecycle in `preCliReworkSetup.js` / `pushReworkChanges.js` (`dmtools-agents`). Evidence: fa PR #1428, 2026-10-09 04:01–05:04Z window — the tick logged **9 arming decisions for one rework push; 8 legs died silently** (no run, no output) while one leg actually worked. Tick log lines: repeated `✅ pr-1428 agent:rework armed` interleaved with `⏭️ ... nothing to rerun`.

## Capability surface

- Arming decision: tick sees unresolved threads / red verdict → arm rework. Must consult an in-flight latch keyed `(pr-number, head-sha)` before dispatching.
- Latch store: fa-state.json on `factory-data` branch (already persists processedKeys) — extend with `reworkInFlight` map.
- Leg completion: rework leg's post-action must report terminal state (pushed / no-changes / failed) so the tick can clear the latch.
- Silent-death handling: a leg that never produced a run must be re-armable after a bounded timeout (not permanently latched).

## Acceptance criteria

1. AC1: while a rework leg for (pr, head) is in flight, the tick's armer logs `⏭️ rework already in flight for (pr, head)` and dispatches nothing.
2. AC2: after the leg terminates (success or failure), the latch clears and a NEW head (new push) re-arms normally.
3. AC3: a latch older than N=45 min with no matching active workflow run is treated as stale and cleared (self-heal, no human).
4. AC4: duplicate reply passes against already-resolved threads are skipped (idempotency: `pr_discussions_raw.json` entries already RESOLVED are filtered before the agent sees them).
5. AC5: unit test in dmtools-agents for the latch filter; tick-side behavior verified on a live fa PR.

## Test plan

- L1: unit tests on the latch map (set/clear/stale-timeout) and resolved-thread filter.
- L2: replay a recorded arming storm (9 identical decisions) against the filter — exactly 1 dispatch.
- L3 (live): one fa GOAL PR cycle — count rework dispatches per push == 1.

## Non-goals

- Changing review-leg verdict semantics (separate card).
- Parallel rework legs (never a goal — serial by design).

## References

- Forensics: fa PR #1428 round-2 window 04:01–05:04Z 2026-10-09 (9 arms / 8 silent deaths).
- Precedents: dmtools-agents #798 (push race), #799 (rework context prep), #802 (diff-text param).

## PR Description

Closes #806
## Root Cause

The SM tick's rework armers (`js/smAgent.js`: `arm_rework`, `fail_validation` re-arm, `conflict_rework`) had no in-flight latch keyed `(pr, head)` — idempotency relied on the `agent:rework` label plus dispatch-time run guards only, so any suppressed dispatch or silently dead leg left the next tick arming the same state again (fa PR #1428: 9 arms / 8 dead legs for one push). Compounding it, `pr_discussions_raw.json` still contained already-RESOLVED threads, inviting duplicate reply passes.

## Fix

- `js/common/reworkLatch.js` (new, pure): latch keyed `pr-<N>@<head-sha>` — arm at decision time; active leg run keeps it, concluded leg run clears it (AC2), no run + 45 min self-heals (AC3); includes the storm dedupe filter.
- `js/smAgent.js`: all three arming paths consult the latch first and log `⏭️ … rework already in flight for (pr-N, head7)` instead of arming (AC1); arms ride the `factory-data` snapshot out.
- `js/factoryState.js`: snapshot carries `reworkInFlight` forward and prunes stale/terminated entries each publish (additive; schema unchanged).
- `js/common/gitOps.js`: `writePRContext` filters `resolved === true` threads before writing `pr_discussions_raw.json` (AC4) — single write site, so every agent sees a clean file.

## Test Coverage

- 53 new tests: `test_reworkLatch.js` (31 — L1 set/clear/stale, L2 nine-decision storm replay → 1 dispatch), `test_factoryState.js` (8 — persistence + pruning), `test_smAgent.js` (11 — AC1/AC2 tick behavior), `test_gitOps.js` (3 — AC4 filter).
- Full suite: **2027 passed, 0 failed** (`dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_all.json`).

## Notes

- Latch clearing is tick-side via the head's Actions runs the tick already queries — no leg-side write; a probe-API failure degrades to age-only checking (fail-safe toward suppressing one extra arm, never toward stacking legs).
- AC5's live check (one fa GOAL PR cycle, dispatches per push == 1) still needs a live factory run; L1/L2 unit coverage is in place.

# gh-806: [BUG] Rework arming has no in-flight latch — one push spawned 9 arming decisions / 8 silently dead legs (fa PR #1428)

## Description

## Goal

Rework arming in the fa factory must be single-flight and idempotent: for a given (PR, head) at most one rework leg may be in flight, and repeat arming decisions for the same state must dedupe instead of stacking legs.

## Subject

The armer in `machine-sm.yml` tick (`fa`) + the rework leg lifecycle in `preCliReworkSetup.js` / `pushReworkChanges.js` (`dmtools-agents`). Evidence: fa PR #1428, 2026-10-09 04:01–05:04Z window — the tick logged **9 arming decisions for one rework push; 8 legs died silently** (no run, no output) while one leg actually worked. Tick log lines: repeated `✅ pr-1428 agent:rework armed` interleaved with `⏭️ ... nothing to rerun`.

## Capability surface

- Arming decision: tick sees unresolved threads / red verdict → arm rework. Must consult an in-flight latch keyed `(pr-number, head-sha)` before dispatching.
- Latch store: fa-state.json on `factory-data` branch (already persists processedKeys) — extend with `reworkInFlight` map.
- Leg completion: rework leg's post-action must report terminal state (pushed / no-changes / failed) so the tick can clear the latch.
- Silent-death handling: a leg that never produced a run must be re-armable after a bounded timeout (not permanently latched).

## Acceptance criteria

1. AC1: while a rework leg for (pr, head) is in flight, the tick's armer logs `⏭️ rework already in flight for (pr, head)` and dispatches nothing.
2. AC2: after the leg terminates (success or failure), the latch clears and a NEW head (new push) re-arms normally.
3. AC3: a latch older than N=45 min with no matching active workflow run is treated as stale and cleared (self-heal, no human).
4. AC4: duplicate reply passes against already-resolved threads are skipped (idempotency: `pr_discussions_raw.json` entries already RESOLVED are filtered before the agent sees them).
5. AC5: unit test in dmtools-agents for the latch filter; tick-side behavior verified on a live fa PR.

## Test plan

- L1: unit tests on the latch map (set/clear/stale-timeout) and resolved-thread filter.
- L2: replay a recorded arming storm (9 identical decisions) against the filter — exactly 1 dispatch.
- L3 (live): one fa GOAL PR cycle — count rework dispatches per push == 1.

## Non-goals

- Changing review-leg verdict semantics (separate card).
- Parallel rework legs (never a goal — serial by design).

## References

- Forensics: fa PR #1428 round-2 window 04:01–05:04Z 2026-10-09 (9 arms / 8 silent deaths).
- Precedents: dmtools-agents #798 (push race), #799 (rework context prep), #802 (diff-text param).

Diff checklist — apply to `pr_diff.txt` For every hunk, ask at least these questions: - [ ] Does the change match the ticket scope? ## PR Description

Closes #806
## Root Cause

The SM tick's rework armers (`js/smAgent.js`: `arm_rework`, `fail_validation` re-arm, `conflict_rework`) had no in-flight latch keyed `(pr, head)` — idempotency relied on the `agent:rework` label plus dispatch-time run guards only, so any suppressed dispatch or silently dead leg left the next tick arming the same state again (fa PR #1428: 9 arms / 8 dead legs for one push). Compounding it, `pr_discussions_raw.json` still contained already-RESOLVED threads, inviting duplicate reply passes.

## Fix

- `js/common/reworkLatch.js` (new, pure): latch keyed `pr-<N>@<head-sha>` — arm at decision time; active leg run keeps it, concluded leg run clears it (AC2), no run + 45 min self-heals (AC3); includes the storm dedupe filter.
- `js/smAgent.js`: all three arming paths consult the latch first and log `⏭️ … rework already in flight for (pr-N, head7)` instead of arming (AC1); arms ride the `factory-data` snapshot out.
- `js/factoryState.js`: snapshot carries `reworkInFlight` forward and prunes stale/terminated entries each publish (additive; schema unchanged).
- `js/common/gitOps.js`: `writePRContext` filters `resolved === true` threads before writing `pr_discussions_raw.json` (AC4) — single write site, so every agent sees a clean file.

## Test Coverage

- 53 new tests: `test_reworkLatch.js` (31 — L1 set/clear/stale, L2 nine-decision storm replay → 1 dispatch), `test_factoryState.js` (8 — persistence + pruning), `test_smAgent.js` (11 — AC1/AC2 tick behavior), `test_gitOps.js` (3 — AC4 filter).
- Full suite: **2027 passed, 0 failed** (`dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_all.json`).

## Notes

- Latch clearing is tick-side via the head's Actions runs the tick already queries — no leg-side write; a probe-API failure degrades to age-only checking (fail-safe toward suppressing one extra arm, never toward stacking legs).
- AC5's live check (one fa GOAL PR cycle, dispatches per push == 1) still needs a live factory run; L1/L2 unit coverage is in place.

# gh-806: [BUG] Rework arming has no in-flight latch — one push spawned 9 arming decisions / 8 silently dead legs (fa PR #1428)

## Description

## Goal

Rework arming in the fa factory must be single-flight and idempotent: for a given (PR, head) at most one rework leg may be in flight, and repeat arming decisions for the same state must dedupe instead of stacking legs.

## Subject

The armer in `machine-sm.yml` tick (`fa`) + the rework leg lifecycle in `preCliReworkSetup.js` / `pushReworkChanges.js` (`dmtools-agents`). Evidence: fa PR #1428, 2026-10-09 04:01–05:04Z window — the tick logged **9 arming decisions for one rework push; 8 legs died silently** (no run, no output) while one leg actually worked. Tick log lines: repeated `✅ pr-1428 agent:rework armed` interleaved with `⏭️ ... nothing to rerun`.

## Capability surface

- Arming decision: tick sees unresolved threads / red verdict → arm rework. Must consult an in-flight latch keyed `(pr-number, head-sha)` before dispatching.
- Latch store: fa-state.json on `factory-data` branch (already persists processedKeys) — extend with `reworkInFlight` map.
- Leg completion: rework leg's post-action must report terminal state (pushed / no-changes / failed) so the tick can clear the latch.
- Silent-death handling: a leg that never produced a run must be re-armable after a bounded timeout (not permanently latched).

## Acceptance criteria

1. AC1: while a rework leg for (pr, head) is in flight, the tick's armer logs `⏭️ rework already in flight for (pr, head)` and dispatches nothing.
2. AC2: after the leg terminates (success or failure), the latch clears and a NEW head (new push) re-arms normally.
3. AC3: a latch older than N=45 min with no matching active workflow run is treated as stale and cleared (self-heal, no human).
4. AC4: duplicate reply passes against already-resolved threads are skipped (idempotency: `pr_discussions_raw.json` entries already RESOLVED are filtered before the agent sees them).
5. AC5: unit test in dmtools-agents for the latch filter; tick-side behavior verified on a live fa PR.

## Test plan

- L1: unit tests on the latch map (set/clear/stale-timeout) and resolved-thread filter.
- L2: replay a recorded arming storm (9 identical decisions) against the filter — exactly 1 dispatch.
- L3 (live): one fa GOAL PR cycle — count rework dispatches per push == 1.

## Non-goals

- Changing review-leg verdict semantics (separate card).
- Parallel rework legs (never a goal — serial by design).

## References

- Forensics: fa PR #1428 round-2 window 04:01–05:04Z 2026-10-09 (9 arms / 8 silent deaths).
- Precedents: dmtools-agents #798 (push race), #799 (rework context prep), #802 (diff-text param).

- **Title**: gh-806 [BUG] Rework arming has no in-flight latch — one push spawned 9 arming decisions / 8 silently dead legs (fa PR #1428)
- **Author**: ai-teammate
- **Branch**: `ai/gh-806` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 10
- **Additions**: +1282
- **Deletions**: -21
- **Created**: 2026-10-09T07:21:01Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-09T07:21:01Z

## PR Description

Closes #806
## Root Cause

The SM tick's rework armers (`js/smAgent.js`: `arm_rework`, `fail_validation` re-arm, `conflict_rework`) had no in-flight latch keyed `(pr, head)` — idempotency relied on the `agent:rework` label plus dispatch-time run guards only, so any suppressed dispatch or silently dead leg left the next tick arming the same state again (fa PR #1428: 9 arms / 8 dead legs for one push). Compounding it, `pr_discussions_raw.json` still contained already-RESOLVED threads, inviting duplicate reply passes.

## Fix

- `js/common/reworkLatch.js` (new, pure): latch keyed `pr-<N>@<head-sha>` — arm at decision time; active leg run keeps it, concluded leg run clears it (AC2), no run + 45 min self-heals (AC3); includes the storm dedupe filter.
- `js/smAgent.js`: all three arming paths consult the latch first and log `⏭️ … rework already in flight for (pr-N, head7)` instead of arming (AC1); arms ride the `factory-data` snapshot out.
- `js/factoryState.js`: snapshot carries `reworkInFlight` forward and prunes stale/terminated entries each publish (additive; schema unchanged).
- `js/common/gitOps.js`: `writePRContext` filters `resolved === true` threads before writing `pr_discussions_raw.json` (AC4) — single write site, so every agent sees a clean file.

## Test Coverage

- 53 new tests: `test_reworkLatch.js` (31 — L1 set/clear/stale, L2 nine-decision storm replay → 1 dispatch), `test_factoryState.js` (8 — persistence + pruning), `test_smAgent.js` (11 — AC1/AC2 tick behavior), `test_gitOps.js` (3 — AC4 filter).
- Full suite: **2027 passed, 0 failed** (`dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_all.json`).

## Notes

- Latch clearing is tick-side via the head's Actions runs the tick already queries — no leg-side write; a probe-API failure degrades to age-only checking (fail-safe toward suppressing one extra arm, never toward stacking legs).
- AC5's live check (one fa GOAL PR cycle, dispatches per push == 1) still needs a live factory run; L1/L2 unit coverage is in place.

# gh-806: [BUG] Rework arming has no in-flight latch — one push spawned 9 arming decisions / 8 silently dead legs (fa PR #1428)

## Description

## Goal

Rework arming in the fa factory must be single-flight and idempotent: for a given (PR, head) at most one rework leg may be in flight, and repeat arming decisions for the same state must dedupe instead of stacking legs.

## Subject

The armer in `machine-sm.yml` tick (`fa`) + the rework leg lifecycle in `preCliReworkSetup.js` / `pushReworkChanges.js` (`dmtools-agents`). Evidence: fa PR #1428, 2026-10-09 04:01–05:04Z window — the tick logged **9 arming decisions for one rework push; 8 legs died silently** (no run, no output) while one leg actually worked. Tick log lines: repeated `✅ pr-1428 agent:rework armed` interleaved with `⏭️ ... nothing to rerun`.

## Capability surface

- Arming decision: tick sees unresolved threads / red verdict → arm rework. Must consult an in-flight latch keyed `(pr-number, head-sha)` before dispatching.
- Latch store: fa-state.json on `factory-data` branch (already persists processedKeys) — extend with `reworkInFlight` map.
- Leg completion: rework leg's post-action must report terminal state (pushed / no-changes / failed) so the tick can clear the latch.
- Silent-death handling: a leg that never produced a run must be re-armable after a bounded timeout (not permanently latched).

## Acceptance criteria

1. AC1: while a rework leg for (pr, head) is in flight, the tick's armer logs `⏭️ rework already in flight for (pr, head)` and dispatches nothing.
2. AC2: after the leg terminates (success or failure), the latch clears and a NEW head (new push) re-arms normally.
3. AC3: a latch older than N=45 min with no matching active workflow run is treated as stale and cleared (self-heal, no human).
4. AC4: duplicate reply passes against already-resolved threads are skipped (idempotency: `pr_discussions_raw.json` entries already RESOLVED are filtered before the agent sees them).
5. AC5: unit test in dmtools-agents for the latch filter; tick-side behavior verified on a live fa PR.

## Test plan

- L1: unit tests on the latch map (set/clear/stale-timeout) and resolved-thread filter.
- L2: replay a recorded arming storm (9 identical decisions) against the filter — exactly 1 dispatch.
- L3 (live): one fa GOAL PR cycle — count rework dispatches per push == 1.

## Non-goals

- Changing review-leg verdict semantics (separate card).
- Parallel rework legs (never a goal — serial by design).

## References

- Forensics: fa PR #1428 round-2 window 04:01–05:04Z 2026-10-09 (9 arms / 8 silent deaths).
- Precedents: dmtools-agents #798 (push race), #799 (rework context prep), #802 (diff-text param).
